changes_made.explanation: No changes needed - all metadata is correctly extracted and properly normalized. The paper clearly addresses NLG (text-to-SQL generation) and all listed items are relevant.

Normalized duplicate metric names to their canonical forms. The paper uses two main metrics: Execution Accuracy and Exact Set Match Accuracy, with various naming variants referring to the same metrics.

Changed answer from Yes to No. The paper uses a verifier/ORM for candidate selection during generation, but this is part of the generation pipeline, not LLM-as-judge evaluation. The ORM is trained specifically for this task, not used as a general evaluator of outputs after generation.
No human evaluation is mentioned in the paper - only automatic metrics are used for evaluation.

overall_notes: The paper presents STaR-SQL, a method for text-to-SQL generation using chain-of-thought reasoning and verification. The extraction was mostly accurate except for Question 3, where the verifier/ORM is used as part of the generation pipeline (candidate selection) rather than as an LLM judge evaluating outputs after generation. The paper focuses on automatic evaluation using execution accuracy and exact match metrics without human evaluation.
